newsitem.title: FRANCE: AGF says needs more details on GAN.
newsitem.headline: AGF says needs more details on GAN.

text.p: France's second largest insurer AGF said on Thursday it needed more details about how the government planned to privatise rival GAN before saying whether it would bid for it.

"It (GAN) has activities which are similar and complement our own," chairman Antoine Jeancourt-Galignani told a news conference at which he announced the insurer's 1996 net profit had jumped 42 percent 1.54 billion francs ($269.3 million).
But he said AGF, which was privatised last year, needed more information about how GAN would be sold before saying it was interested in the state-controlled insurer.
"We have to know how, when and under what conditions it (the government) plans to privatise it," he said. "The privatisation decree hasn't been issued yet."
"We're observing things," he said. "When the government moves, we will carry out our reflection...we're watching with enormous interest what is happening."

The merger announced last year between French insurers Axa and UAP, creating the world's second largest insurance group, has triggered market speculation about further consolidation in the French sector.

AGF chairman said GAN's new management had made a "very complete inventory of the losses and problems of GAN which are considerable" and that GAN could look forward to a future as a "normal player" in the insurance sector.
The centre-right government has said it will pay at least 20 billion francs to cover GAN's losses and ready it for sale. It plans to sell GAN this year.
GAN was badly hit by France's property slump as well by an ill-fated policy of cutting insurance premiums.

Published reports have said privatisation of the principal operating businesses of GAN -- UIC, its property lending arm, GAN Assurances, its insurance division, and CIC, its regional banking network, could begin in the next three months.
Referring to speculation AGF itself could be a bid target, the chairman said any bid launched for the insurer would be a hostile one.
"An offer for us would be hostile. We do not consider a takeover to be in the interest of our shareholders," he said.

There has been widespread market speculation that German insurer Allianz ALVD.F might bid for AGF. But Allianz, which wants to boost its French presence, indicated on Wednesday that it was more interested in GAN.
At the same time, the AGF chairman did not rule out alliances or partnships with other European companies.
He said the merger between Axa and UAP had accelerated consolidation in the sector and AGF could not sit on the sidelines.
